title: The elements.
lede: The first twenty elements and the pub-quiz regulars from further along: their symbols and atomic numbers, sorted by family, with the table filling in as I learn them.

card.title: The elements
card.desc: Thirty-nine elements, their symbols and atomic numbers, on a periodic table that fills in as I learn.

map.label: symbol
map.hint: Point at an element to see it. They fill in as I master them.

questions.ask: Which element has this atomic number?

groups.label: Non-metals
groups.note: The stuff of air, water and life itself: everything you're made of is mostly these six.

groups.label: Noble gases
groups.note: The far right-hand column: so content with themselves they barely react with anything.

groups.label: Halogens
groups.note: Next door to the noble gases, and the opposite temperament: fiercely reactive.

groups.label: Alkali metals
groups.note: The far left-hand column: soft, shiny, and inclined to explode in water.

groups.label: Alkaline earth metals
groups.note: Column two: the alkali metals' calmer neighbours.

groups.label: Transition metals
groups.note: The wide middle of the table, home of most of the metals you could name.

groups.label: Other metals
groups.note: Softer, humbler metals tucked in to the right of the transition block.

groups.label: Metalloids
groups.note: Half metal, half not, along the staircase that divides the table.

groups.label: Actinides
groups.note: The bottom row: heavy, radioactive, and best admired from a distance.

items.name: Sodium
items.hook: Na is for natrium, from natron: the salty soda the Egyptians used to dry out their mummies.

items.name: Potassium
items.hook: K is for kalium, from the Arabic for plant ash, where it was first found. Potash gives us “potassium”.

items.name: Iron
items.hook: Fe is ferrum, the Latin for iron, hence “ferrous”. The Ferris wheel is a coincidence, named after a Mr Ferris.

items.name: Copper
items.hook: Cu is cuprum, after Cyprus, which supplied the Roman world with its copper.

items.name: Silver
items.hook: Ag is argentum, the Latin for silver. Argentina was named for it, in hope rather than in fact.

items.name: Tungsten
items.hook: W is wolfram, from the German: the ore ate up tin in the smelter like a wolf. “Tungsten” is Swedish for heavy stone.

items.name: Gold
items.hook: Au is aurum, the Latin for gold. Say “Ay, you!” at anyone wearing too much of it.

items.name: Mercury
items.hook: Hg is hydrargyrum, Greek for “water-silver”: a metal that's liquid at room temperature.

items.name: Tin
items.hook: Sn is stannum, the Latin for tin. Cornwall's tin miners had their own courts, the Stannaries.

items.name: Lead
items.hook: Pb is plumbum, the Latin for lead. Roman water pipes were lead, so the person who fixes them is a plumber.

items.name: Antimony
items.hook: Sb is stibium, the black eye make-up the ancient Egyptians ground from its ore.
